topic: Every exponent rule from one idea

scenes.title: Wstęp
scenes.purpose: Hook with five familiar exponent rules and promise a single reason.
scenes.mathematicalConcept: a^m·a^n, (a^m)^n, a^0, a^-n and a^(1/n) look like five separate rules.
scenes.animation: Title writes on, five rules fade in, each is pulsed, subtitle lands.
scenes.text: SKĄD SIĘ BIORĄ WSZYSTKIE REGUŁY POTĘG?

scenes.title: Plan
scenes.purpose: Expose the repetitive structure of the video up front.
scenes.mathematicalConcept: Observe one law, run it on many cases, then show why it can never fail.
scenes.animation: Chapter list fades in row by row; the worked-examples entry is boxed and pulsed.

scenes.title: Podstawy
scenes.purpose: Pin down: base, exponent as a factor count, and the running product.
scenes.mathematicalConcept: a^n means a written as a factor n times; the running product of 2^4 ticks 2, 4, 8, 16.
scenes.animation: 2^4 unfolds into 2·2·2·2; a counter runs 2, 4, 8, 16 as each factor lands; base and exponent are labelled.

scenes.title: Główna budowa
scenes.purpose: Show the whole idea once, slowly: 2^3 · 2^2 is three 2s then two more, five factors.
scenes.mathematicalConcept: 2^3·2^2 = 2^(3+2) = 2^5; exponents add because factors are appended.
scenes.animation: Two strips slide together into one strip of five; the exponent line and the numeric check land; the law a^m·a^n = a^(m+n) is stated.

scenes.title: Przykład 1 — 2^2 · 2^3
scenes.purpose: Worked case 1 of 8, identical template: 2^2 · 2^3 = 2^5.
scenes.mathematicalConcept: Multiplying 2^2 by 2^3 lays m factors then n more: 2 + 3 = 5 factors, so the product is 2^5.
scenes.animation: The shared example template: two factor strips, slide them together, brace the total, exponents add, check the plain number, log the ledger row.
scenes.camera: Static landscape frame, strips on the left, worked lines and ledger on the right.
scenes.transition: Cut to the next example, same layout.

scenes.title: Sprawdzenie wzoru
scenes.purpose: Read the pattern back off the eight results: the answer's exponent is the sum of the two.
scenes.mathematicalConcept: In every worked line, the exponent on the right equals the sum of the two exponents on the left.
objects: stacked list of the eight products
scenes.animation: The eight products stack up; the two left exponents and the right exponent are boxed and shown to satisfy m + n = result.

scenes.title: Duży przypadek
scenes.purpose: Stress-test the law far from the small cases: 2^10 · 2^15 = 2^25.
scenes.mathematicalConcept: Ten factors then fifteen more is twenty-five factors; 1024 · 32768 = 33 554 432 = 2^25.
scenes.animation: A strip of ten and a strip of fifteen slide together into twenty-five; braces count 10, 15, 25; the plain number checks out.

scenes.title: Dlaczego to działa
scenes.purpose: Show, generically, that the step can never fail: m factors and n factors are m + n factors by definition.
scenes.mathematicalConcept: a^m is m factors, a^n is n factors; concatenation gives m + n factors, so a^m·a^n = a^(m+n).
scenes.animation: A generic a-strip of m and one of n slide together; braces read m, n, then m+n; the identity is written and circled.
scenes.text: m czynników + n czynników = (m + n) czynników

scenes.title: Jedno prawo, każda reguła
scenes.purpose: Derive (a^m)^n, a^0 and a^-n as the only choices that keep 'exponents add' true.
scenes.mathematicalConcept: (a^m)^n = a^(mn); a^0 = 1 forced by a^m·a^0 = a^m; a^-n = 1/a^n forced by a^n·a^-n = 1.
scenes.animation: Three panels fade in one at a time; each states the requirement, then the forced value, then a numeric check.

scenes.title: Pierwiastek jako wykładnik 1/n
scenes.purpose: Force a^(1/n) to be the n-th root by the power-of-a-power law.
scenes.mathematicalConcept: (a^(1/n))^n = a^(n·1/n) = a^1 = a, so a^(1/n) is the number whose n-th power is a.
scenes.animation: The requirement (a^(1/n))^n = a is written, the conclusion 'n-th root' lands, three cases check out.

scenes.title: Algebra
scenes.purpose: Collect every rule as a one-line consequence of a^m·a^n = a^(m+n).
scenes.mathematicalConcept: From the additive law: (a^m)^n = a^mn, a^0 = 1, a^-n = 1/a^n, a^(1/n) = n-th root, a^m/a^n = a^(m-n).
scenes.animation: The law is written large; five derived rules fade in beneath, each tagged 'from adding exponents'.
scenes.text: aᵐ · aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ  →  every other rule

scenes.title: Podsumowanie
scenes.purpose: Restate the worked cases and the single reason behind them.
scenes.mathematicalConcept: Every worked case is one instance of a^m·a^n = a^(m+n); every rule follows from it.
scenes.animation: The case ledger rebuilds, the strip merges once more, and the reason line lands.

scenes.title: Koniec
scenes.purpose: Hold the one law and the five rules it produces.
scenes.mathematicalConcept: a^m·a^n = a^(m+n) is the whole content; the rest is reading it in different directions.
scenes.animation: The law holds; the five rules fade in small beneath it; the tagline lands.
